entries.english: In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity. Since events are liable to fade from memory, they must be preserved in writing and by witnesses. Margaret, lady of the Kingdom of Bohemia, duchess of Austria and Styria, and margravine of Moravia, makes known that, having learned Wok von Rosenberg’s faithful character by experience and especially considering his nobility, since he comes from free and noble forebears and can therefore hold counties or higher dignities if bestowed on him, and with the consent and express will of her husband, the illustrious King of Bohemia, she has granted to Wok and his heirs after him, forever and as a fief, the county of Retz with its rights: the patronage of churches in that county, beneficed men and those holding fiefs there, courts and advocacies belonging to the county, dowers commonly called *lipgedinge*, pledged possessions that are to revert to the county in due course, and all other rights by whatever name. This grant is made without condition or exception. She ordered this charter written and sealed. Witnesses present were Philipp, elect of Salzburg; Bruno, Bischof zu Olmütz; Otto, Marggraf zu Brandenburg; Ulrich, Herzog zu Kärnten; Heinrich, Herzog zu Polen; the younger brothers Werenhard and Heinrich de Schowenberch; Heinrich, Burggraf de Dewin; Hoyerius de Vridberch; Gerossius, Burggraf zu Prag; Zmilo de Lewchtenberch; Ratmir de Phremperch; Hermann de Richnawe; Bavarus de Strakonitz; Ulrich genannt Lepus; Wilhelm de Bodebrade; Burkhard de Klingenberch; Sdezlaus de Sternberch; Bvdiwoy de Zcaliz; Hoyerius de Swinz; Ulrich de Novadomo; Heinrich von Lichtenstein; Otto de Meysow; Otto de Haslaw; and very many others. Enacted at La, and given in the tents by Morava in the year of the Lord 1260. The charter is elegantly written without lines and has suffered damp damage; the bracketed words were supplied from an old copy. The badly crumbled seal in white wax hangs from red silk; the right half is lost except for a small part. It may show a seated female figure, with the surviving inscription “Margareta ... by the grace of God duchess ...”. A short version appears in Kurz, Ölt. Alb. II, 175, no. 2.
